title: Proteins identified in pooled sera of B. canis canis dogs (admission, day 1, day 6) and healthy dogs (2DE spots, MS/MS)
licence: article licence (Europe PMC open-access record); not separately specified
raw_vs_processed: processed (published protein identification tables for six gel spots from pooled sera; no raw spectra, gel quantification or per-dog data)
n_animals_basis: not applicable (no per-animal rows). The tables describe pooled sera. The dump does not state how many dogs went into each pool. The article note gives 25 infected and 10 healthy dogs overall (cohort CH22, shared with CB011).
files_summary: Zip of 12 members. 4 Word files (Additional files 1-4), each with one table of 6 rows (header plus spots 596, 579, 432, 590, 869, 327): S1 = B. canis dogs at admission, S2 = day 1, S3 = day 6, S4 = healthy dogs. Columns: spot number, protein name, NCBI gi accession, theoretical Mr/pI, unique peptides, sequence coverage %, Mascot score. By my count that is 24 spot rows and 64 protein entries (S1 16, S2 12, S3 21, S4 15), covering 19 distinct protein names (18 if the two albumin names are merged). The other 8 members are 4 JPG and 4 GIF image files (figures, likely duplicates in two formats; not read). Article DOI 10.1186/1746-6148-10-111.
suitable_questions: Not suitable for animal-level analysis; usable only as published protein identification lists (which proteins were found in six pooled-serum gel spots at each time point and in healthy dogs). Useful as a candidate-marker list (acute-phase, complement, coagulation, apolipoprotein and vitamin D-binding proteins) to guide targeted assays, not for statistics, modelling or group comparisons of abundance.
unverified_fields: licence (article-level only; the dump states none)
number of dogs in each pool (not in the supplement; 25 infected and 10 healthy come from the article note)

per-protein peptide, coverage and Mascot values: table cells of multi-protein spots are run together without separators (for example '1863', '531115', '372218114'), so values can only be split with the article's printed table; the full-text snippet also splits some numbers ambiguously (for example S1 spot 590 '66 42 72 62 1401 836')
agreement with the article's Table 2 (note says 17 proteins; I count 19 distinct names across the four files, 18 if the two albumin names are merged; Table 2 was not available to me)
content of the 8 image files (JPG/GIF; only file headers were seen, so the figure content and the duplicate-format guess are unconfirmed)
which of the 6 spots match the 64/49/37 differential spots in the article (the supplement covers only the six identified spots)
SHA-256 and file download details not checked here (from the inspection summary only)
